author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Commissioner said Shenzhen Qingcheng, the app maker behind the HeyCyan app in the smartglasses, failed to respond to her inquiries

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian privacy regulator has opened an investigation into the China-based software company behind the HeyCyan app in Kmart’s $89 smartglasses, following public outrage over the covert use of the devices.

In August, Guardian Australia reported Kmart had sold out of the Anko-branded discount version of Meta’s smartglasses that can capture images and record high-definition video, which led to widespread concern and calls to ban or
title: Privacy watchdog launches probe into China-based company behind Kmart ‘pervert glasses’ app

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Manager who removed Macdonald announces she will replace the late James Valentine from March

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two years after her shock axing, the ABC has backflipped and reinstated ABC Radio presenter Sarah Macdonald to Sydney’s local radio schedule, where she will replace the late James Valentine from March.

The manager who had removed Macdonald without explanation, ABC director of audio Ben Latimer, announced her return on Wednesday to take on the afternoons slot.

Continue reading...
title: Sarah Macdonald returns to ABC radio after being sacked in 2024

author: Roque Planas and Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
As Angelenos bemoan ‘sad situation’, those in San Diego say remark a ‘disservice’ to town with multiple naval bases

Donald Trump’s extraordinary implication that Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego have sparked condemnation across the political spectrum. As residents of the two major west coast cities awoke on Tuesday to another sweltering day in a record-breaking heatwave, the president’s comments sent blood boiling even higher.

Jessica, a 28-year-old Los Angeles hair stylist, was scrolling through social media early on Tuesday morning and was shocked to see that Trump had just suggested Iran should decimate her home town.

Continue reading...
title: LA and San Diego residents ‘horrified’ by Trump’s comment: ‘obsessed with us’

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo in Los Angeles
description:
Several cities shatter temperatures for time of year as extreme heat warnings in place along California coast

An unprecedented heatwave has gripped southern California, boosting temperatures 15 to 20 degrees above normal for autumn.

Monday was a notably sweltering day for several cities.

Continue reading...
title: Record high temperatures as southern California swelters under heatwave

author: Maya Yang
description:
First hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 1905 as scientists say possible US landfall on Saturday

Tropical Depression Nine has been predicted to be the Atlantic season’s first hurricane and potentially the latest first hurricane to develop in over a century.

The system was located Tuesday afternoon about 630 miles south-west of the mouth of the Mississippi River, with maximum sustained winds of 35 mph, according to the US National Hurricane Center.

Continue reading...
title: Tropical depression in Gulf predicted to be Atlantic season’s first hurricane

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
President floats idea as voter anger over rising costs threatens Republican hopes in November midterms

Donald Trump said on Tuesday his administration was considering suspending the federal gasoline tax, a sign the president is noticing voter anger over fuel costs a month before the midterm elections.

“We’re thinking about that,” Trump said when asked whether the tax should be suspended.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says he is weighing suspension of federal gas tax

author: Lauren Aratani
description:
S&P tops 7,800 for first time in history as investors optimistic despite signs of instability in US economy

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at a record high after a rally around AI chipmakers and a dip in US treasury yields.

At market’s close, the S&P 500 was up 0.58%, topping 7,800 for the first time in its history. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index rose 0.45%, while the Dow, which is slightly down from its record high in August, climbed 0.49%.

Continue reading...
title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq surge to record highs after AI chipmaker rally

author: Emma Graham-Harrison and Quique Kierszenbaum in Nir Oz
description:
Israeli communities shattered by Hamas masacres are torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives

Keith Siegel spent many of his long hours in Hamas captivity in Gaza etching everything that happened after 7 October 2023 into his memory. For 484 days, he recited to himself every place he was held, the dates he was moved and every attack or humiliation he endured or witnessed.

He aimed to store intelligence that could help Israeli forces free other hostages if he was released, to keep track of time as the days slid by and be able to tell his family what happened to him. Now his body is free, but he cannot loosen those memories.

Continue reading...
title: ‘All I want to do is cry’: trauma of 7 October survivors three years after the attacks

author: Richard Adams Education editor
description:
Letter signed by more than 40 signatories say Cambridge has backed away from promised thorough review of events before Arday’s death

Senior Cambridge academics have criticised the university’s plans to investigate Prof Jason Arday’s death as inadequate, and said those responsible for “serious failures of leadership” should face consequences.

In a letter to Chris Smith, Cambridge’s chancellor, the academics said “it is not yet clear” how the proposed review will answer difficult questions about the university’s involvement in the events leading up to Arday’s death, including its handling of the criticism Arday suffered after his appointment as professor of sociology of education in 2023.

Continue reading...
title: Cambridge academics say university’s plans to investigate Jason Arday’s death are inadequate

author: Associated Press
description:
Silvia Zhang and Guojun Xuan had 15 children, aged between two months to 13 years, removed from their home

A California couple has been arrested on child abuse charges following an investigation into a surrogacy scheme involving at least 21 kids, police said on Tuesday.

Silvia Zhang and her husband, Guojun Xuan are expected to face conspiracy to commit child abuse charges, according to the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department.

Continue reading...
title: California couple charged with child abuse in surrogacy scheme involving at least 21 kids

author: Shrai Popat in Washington
description:
The White House denies the allegations as ‘false’ and says the ‘first amendment does not protect violent rioting’

  • US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump ordered the FBI to investigate protesters in Los Angeles who were demonstrating against the president’s immigration crackdown, according to a whistleblower complaint.

US senator Alex Padilla, a Democrat who represents California and serves on the Senate judiciary committee, said his office had received a copy of the complaint, which makes sweeping allegations about the Trump administration’s response to protests in LA in early 2025.

Continue reading...
title: Whistleblower suit alleges Trump ordered FBI investigation on LA anti-ICE protesters

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Former and current officials who bolstered claims of voter fraud in 2020 make fresh allegations of vulnerabilities

Prominent election deniers have spent recent weeks stoking fears over US election security before next month’s midterms, echoing claims pushed by Donald Trump to justify asserting more control over voting.

On conservative-friendly media outlets, former or current officials who tried to bolster the US president’s false claims of mass voter fraud in 2020 have in recent weeks made fresh allegations of election vulnerabilities.

Continue reading...
title: Election deniers stoke Trump-driven ballot security fears before midterms

author: Victoria Bekiempis in New York
description:
Klara Shuster said in court she imported mislabeled Botox illegally and dispensed it to clients

The owner of a New York City med spa has admitted to illegally administering bootleg Botox, which authorities say led one client to develop botulism.

Klara Shuster, also known as Klara Chrzuszcz, made those admissions in the course of pleading guilty in federal court recently to conspiracy to commit smuggling, among other charges.

Continue reading...
title: New York City med spa owner admits to giving client botulism with bootleg Botox

author: Shrai Popat and David Smith in Washington
description:
Congressional candidate Jim Desmond says he ‘served to protect Americans, not write off American cities’

A Republican candidate in San Diego has criticized Donald Trump after the US president suggested Iran could “take out” the city or Los Angeles.

Trump has faced a chorus of condemnation from Democratic leaders in California after his comments at a rally in Nebraska on Monday night. Republicans have largely remained silent.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s suggestion to ‘take out’ LA or San Diego draws Republican rebuke

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Sarah Pochin bought Anglesey property two days after writing to minister about impact of second home ownership on rural communities

A Reform UK MP bought an £800,000 second home on a picturesque Welsh island two days after raising concerns in parliament about the impact of second homes on rural communities.

Sarah Pochin completed the purchase of a Grade-II listed property on the southern coast of Anglesey (Ynys Môn).

Continue reading...
title: Reform MP raises concerns about second homes – then buys one for £800,000

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
Enlargement commissioner Marta Kos outlines proposed safeguards to protect EU from undemocratic leaders

The European Commission wants to ensure there is no repeat Viktor Orbán among the next generation of EU member states, as it set out plans to prepare for the bloc’s enlargement into eastern Europe in the next few years.

In an interview with the Guardian and other European newspapers, the EU commissioner for enlargement, Marta Kos, outlined proposals for special safeguards to protect the bloc from leaders who could flout democratic values and hold hostage decision making, a pattern of behaviour exemplified for many by the former Hungarian prime minister.

Continue reading...
title: ‘No more Viktor Orbán: EU plans 15-year probation period for new member states

author: Associated Press
description:
CBP says in response to lawsuit use-of-force cases are ‘thoroughly investigated, reviewed, and presented’

A US citizen who was shot one year ago by a Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agent during a sweeping immigration crackdown in Chicago filed a lawsuit against the federal government on Monday, alleging the agent lied about the shooting and fired into her vehicle from behind.

Federal prosecutors initially accused Marimar Martinez, then 30, of using her vehicle to strike and box in agent Charles Exum’s sport utility vehicle on Chicago’s south-west side on 4 October 2025 during what the Trump administration named Operation Midway Blitz. Exum then exited his car and opened fire, leaving Martin
title: US citizen alleges immigration agent in Chicago shot her from behind

author: Christopher Knaus and Ariel Bogle
description:
‘All deceased persons should be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their financial circumstances,’ authorities say after Guardian Australia investigation

  • Find more from the Unmarked graves investigation here

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has been urged to use national cabinet to stop the use of unmarked communal graves to bury impoverished Australians and address failings that are leaving family and friends blindsided.

Guardian Australia’s revelations on Tuesday that unmarked, communal graves were being used, in some cases without notifying the families of the deceased, prompted widespread po
title: PM called on to act on communal grave revelations as NSW commits to urgent review

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Angus Taylor’s drastic cuts to graduate visas aim to end a citizenship pathway, but universities body says changes will make Australia less competitive

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Coalition’s migration plan risks breaching Australia’s free trade agreement with India, signed by the former Morrison government, allowing Indian students to stay and work for up to four years after completing their studies.

Angus Taylor on Tuesday announced plans to cut net overseas migration to 100,000 for the first two years of a Coalition government and up to 160,000 in year four, in a plan which
title: Coalition’s migration plan risks breaching India free trade agreement and damaging economy, advocates warn

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Industry leaders say bogus claims rose 14% last year, pushing up premiums for all customers

An insurance fraudster who pocketed more than £14,000 for the supposed theft of Lego sets, fishing gear and gaming consoles was behind one of last year’s most high-profile bogus claims.

Investigators uncovered £1.34bn of fraud in 2025, a 14% increase on the year before, according to the Association of British Insurers (ABI).

Continue reading...
title: Lego collector’s insurance scam highlights UK’s £1.3bn fraud problem

author: Jimmy Tobias
description:
John Murdock had been working for the agency for 18 years and his resignation comes during an exodus of longtime federal workers and scientists

An 18-year veteran of the US Department of Interior has resigned in protest from the sprawling federal agency, denouncing “a deeply troubling assault on the rule of the law” that took place at the department under Donald Trump.

John Murdock, an attorney and self-described conservative Christian, began working for the agency’s legal office in 2002. In his resignation letter, first sent to his supervisor earlier this year and obtained exclusively by the Guardian and Public Domain, Murdock cites “glaring legal flaws” he witnessed within the agency during the course of the Trump administration, as well as concerns over offshore oil and gas drilling, the aggressive push to expand fossil fuels and the flouting of environmental regulation.
title: Veteran conservative lawyer quits Trump’s interior department and warns of ‘assault on the rule of law’

author: Martin Belam
description:
California’s leaders attack president after he suggests Iran could ‘take out’ Los Angeles or San Diego. Plus an auction of some of the most famous props in movie history

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Donald Trump has suggested Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego, in comments described as “reckless” and “deranged” by California officials. At a rally in Nebraska on Monday, the crowd applauded when the US president said high prices owing to the war with Iran were a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe – keeping our country safe”. He added: “They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.”

Gavin Newsom, the
title: ‘Deranged’ and ‘dangerous’ Trump calls for Iran to strike US cities amid historic ratings low | First Thing

author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
description:
Pablo Quirno says move is part of government’s strategy to peacefully assert sovereignty over the islands

Argentina’s foreign minister has told an audience that included the British ambassador that his government would stop the Falkland Islands from exploiting its offshore oilfields as part of a strategy to take sovereignty.

During a speech at a thinktank event in the Argentinian capital, Pablo Quirno condemned the British government for failing to open negotiations over the islands and facilitating a significant offshore oil project in its waters.

Continue reading...
title: Argentina to stop Falklands exploiting offshore oilfields, country’s foreign minister says

author: Josh Butler
description:
Jason Kwon’s answers were provided in a helpful, quiet and calm manner. For a company under intense scrutiny, there were no missteps

Open AI’s Jason Kwon flew 15 hours from San Francisco to Sydney to give the company’s first in-person mea culpa after it admitted – in an unsigned email, to a public departmental inbox – that one of its AI agents had accessed a Services Australia website without authorisation and grabbed data related to Medicare.

Kwon – polite, friendly, even-toned – got through a potentially dicey committee hearing unscathed, promising to do better and pledging assistance to Australia. No missteps, no viral moments, just delivering his answers helpfully, in a quiet and calm manner, sympathising with the questioner and the point they were making.
title: OpenAI delivers a mea culpa to the Australian government in person – but answers still elude

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Polls show GOP candidates trailing Democrats in Senate races, and Republicans also struggling in House contests

Thirty days remain until the midterm elections, and Donald Trump and his Republican allies are pulling out all the stops to maintain control of Congress.

Super Pacs aligned with the GOP have already spent hundreds of millions of dollars on advertising and voter outreach in races expected to decide the majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives, and plan to spend even more before the election is over. The president, vice-president JD Vance, and other top Republicans are fanning out across the country to stump for vulnerable lawmakers.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats upbeat as unpopular Trump imperils Republican midterm hopes

author: Guardian staff
description:
Michael Rowland and Leigh Sales lead tributes to newsreader who read the ABC’s 7pm bulletin for 20 years

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Former ABC news presenter Richard Morecroft has died at the age of 70.

Morecroft presented ABC’s 7pm news bulletin for almost 20 years until 2002.

Continue reading...
title: Richard Morecroft, veteran ABC news presenter, dies age 70 after cancer diagnosis

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Campaign group’s analysis of North Yorkshire plans finds datacentre would have to burn 4.9m tonnes of wood a year

Drax’s planned datacentre could produce nearly double the emissions of all flights out of Gatwick airport each year by burning 4.9m tonnes of wood annually, an analysis has shown.

Campaigners say this would make it “one of the dirtiest datacentres out there”.

Continue reading...
title: Drax datacentre could create nearly twice the yearly emissions of all Gatwick flights

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Push message claims fashion company’s data has been ‘fully compromised’, but website and app remain online

  • Business live – latest updates

Asos is investigating after users of its mobile app received a notification claiming hackers had “fully compromised” the online fashion retailer’s data.

The value of Asos’s shares on the London Stock Exchange dived almost 12%, after thousands of customers received a mobile app notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link which sent them to the Telegram messaging service.

Continue reading...
title: Asos customers receive ‘hack’ notification threatening leak

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
President claims commercials were ‘positive promotion for our Great USA’ but says he will now cover their cost

  • Sign up for Breaking News US email

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Donald Trump has said he will stop using taxpayer funds for television advertisements glorifying himself, which sparked a major backlash, and instead tap his super PAC to cover ads going forward.

Donald Trump said he was “doing great” as his approval rating sank to a record low 32%. The president made the remarks as he headed to Nebraska, to campaign for a Republican senator there.

Pennsylvania is reporting the largest measles ou
title: Trump says he will stop using taxpayer funds for self-promoting ads after backlash – US politics live

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Watchdog examining whether company carried out adequate risk assessment as required by Online Safety Act

Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is under investigation for a potential breach of the UK’s digital safety laws after launching a Snapchat-style feature on Instagram.

The UK’s communications watchdog, Ofcom, is investigating whether the $1.9tn (£1.4tn) company infringed the Online Safety Act (OSA) by failing to carry out adequate checks on whether its Instagram Instants product could show illegal content or be accessed by children.

Continue reading...
title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants safety checks

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
She must decide by the end of the week whether to seek further review of federal charges over a confrontation with ICE agents at Delaney Hall

A US congresswoman who just gave birth to a baby girl faces a deadline this week on whether to seek a rehearing of a federal case against her by the Trump administration after an oversight visit to an immigration detention facility.

LaMonica McIver, 40, represents New Jersey’s 10th congressional district. She gave birth to her second child last Thursday – a rarity for a sitting member of Congress. She is only the 15th member of Congress to give birth while serving and part of a small subset of congresswomen who have school-age children.

Continue reading...
title: New Jersey congresswoman LaMonica McIver faces legal deadline after giving birth to second child

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Police say body found by trail bike riders at remote farm in Terragon is badly decomposed, sparking search of missing persons records

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A partially submerged body believed to be a woman has been discovered in a remote stockyard, with the death being treated as suspicious.

Officers were called to a property in Terragon, near Murwillumbah in northern NSW, at about 11.20am on Monday after reports of a dead body.

Continue reading...
title: Woman’s body found in stockyard trough close to NSW-Queensland border

author: Maya Yang
description:
For-profit water corporations, federal cuts and climate crisis are ‘supercharging water rate hikes’, study co-author says

US households are paying 62% more for drinking water than they did a decade ago – outpacing inflation, grocery prices and household incomes, according to a new study.

Food & Water Watch, a Washington DC-based non-profit, analyzed 2025 billing data from the 500 largest community water systems in the US, which together serve about 155 million people, or 45% of the country’s population. The analysis compared current rates with data from a similar Food & Water Watch survey conducted in 2015. The study does not include wastewater or storm water charges, which are often billed separately from drinking water service.

Continue reading...
title: US households pay 62% more for water than they did a decade ago, study finds

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
Labour could pay price for disappearance of parks and playgrounds around Euston station

When HS2 construction began around London’s Euston station in 2017 and people living nearby watched parks and playgrounds give way to diggers and rubble, they were promised that the lost green space would be replaced. “They have to give it all back,” said Dorothea Hackman. “But they are destroying it – so there’s nothing to give back.”

As the dust from the political party conference season begins to settle, disappearing green spaces and housing developments have become central issues in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection. On Thursday, Labour and the Green party will contest the seismic seat vacated by the former prime minster Keir Starmer.

Continue reading...
title: Loss of green space could be issue that decides Holborn and St Pancras byelection

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Excluive: Weapon is one of hundreds of items to be sold as part of the influential late director’s personal archive

The axe wielded by Jack Nicholson as he delivered his chillingly manic line “Here’s Johnny!” in the 1980 horror movie The Shining is to go on sale.

Nicholson’s character, Jack Torrance, uses the axe to hack out an opening in a locked door protecting his terrified wife Wendy, played by Shelley Duvall. It is also the murder weapon in the killing of Scatman Crothers’ character, Dick Hallorann. One of cinema’s most famous axes could be yours for a list price of between £30,000 and £50,000.

Continue reading...
title: The Shining axe used by Jack Nicholson for sale as part Stanley Kubrick auction

author: Associated Press in Berlin
description:
August Hanning served as president of Federal Intelligence Service from 1998 to 2005

Germany’s federal prosecutor’s office has said a former domestic intelligence chief was arrested on Tuesday on espionage allegations.

August Hanning served as president of the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from December 1998 to November 2005.

Continue reading...
title: Germany arrests former domestic intelligence chief over alleged spying

author: Reuters
description:
Bakker spent four and a half years in prison after being convicted in 1989 ​of defrauding followers in a scheme involving holidays at his Christian theme park

The US televangelist Jim Bakker, who built a multimillion-dollar empire and lived ⁠in opulence before being disgraced by a sex scandal, a conviction for defrauding followers and divorce from his television co-host Tammy Faye, has died aged 86.

The death of Bakker, whose journey from the TV pulpit to a prison cell in the 1980s inspired comparisons to the corrupt character of the fictional preacher-huckster Elmer Gantry, was revealed on ⁠social media by his second wife, Lori ⁠Bakker.

Continue reading...
title: US televangelist Jim Bakker, ensnared in fraud and sex scandal, dies at 86

author: Reuters in Nairobi
description:
Health minister says 28 contacts identified after death of citizen who arrived from DRC on Saturday

Kenya ⁠has recorded its ⁠first confirmed ​Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic ⁠Republic of the Congo and arrived in Nairobi on Saturday, the health minister, Aden ⁠Duale, has said.

The patient has since died, ​and 28 contacts ‌have been identified ‌so far including family members and health ‌workers, Duale told a press conference.

Continue reading...
title: Kenya confirms first Ebola case and says patient has died

author: Tom McIlroy
description:
Coalition leader’s proposal goes further than Peter Dutton’s 2025 election promise and beyond even Pauline Hanson’s bottom line

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

With Angus Taylor’s hardline immigration policy unveiled on Tuesday, voters have a new measure of Pauline Hanson’s success in dragging politics further to the right.

Taylor’s plan will cut 60,000 more people from net overseas migration (Nom) than the reductions proposed by Peter Dutton just before the 2025 election. Dutton wanted to take Nom down to
title: Taylor’s hardline immigration plan drags Australian politics further to the right – and it’s all upside for One Nation

author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
Relations have soured between the two countries over a number of issues since 2023, but Hillel Newman says a ‘reset’ is possible

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Israel’s ambassador to Australia says the third anniversary of October 7 is an opportunity for both countries to return to “traditional friendship”.

But, in the lead-up to commemorations on Wednesday marking Hamas’ terror attack, leaders of Australia’s Palestinian community say the federal government should do more to help the diaspora suffering since the war on Gaza.

Sign up for Guar
title: Israeli ambassador to Australia says he hopes for return to ‘traditional friendship’ on October 7 anniversary eve

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Conservatives plan ‘new integrated air and missile defence system to protect Britain from attack – in essence, a British “Iron Dome”’

The Liberal Democrats have dismissed the Tory plan for a “Britannia Shield” as “Truss-style fantasy economics”. They say the Conservatives would only get a “Patchwork Dome” with the £10bn they plan to spend on the project.

James MacCleary, the Lib Dem defence spokesperson, said:

Once again the Conservatives are indulging in Truss-style fantasy economics. £10bn would not even touch the sides for a complete UK-wide ‘Iron Dome’. They either need to review their dodgy sums or come clean about which parts of the country their Patchwork Dome wouldn’t cover.

Let’s not forget this is the party that hollowed out our armed forces for a decade, and whose disgraceful plan to fill the defence-spending black hole is based on targeted cuts to the poorest and most vulnerable children. You do not make Britain
title: Badenoch calls for UK ‘Iron Dome’ missile defence system - UK politics live

author: Niha Masih
description:
The country’s 85-medal haul included athletes who trained with limited money and borrowed equipment. Plus, the Mumbai performer turning everyday absurdities into comedy

In a country where cricket eclipses every other sport, the recently concluded Asian Games offered a much-needed reminder of India’s breadth of sporting talent. In this edition of the games, in Japan, India won 85 medals: 21 golds, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. I admit I did not know many of the players competing, or even some of the sports they play before putting this piece together. Learning about the stories, I wonder why not.

There were individual breakthroughs, records broken and history made. There were also hard-fought team victories, including the Indian
title: From competing for food to a gold medal: the stories behind India’s Asian Games winners

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Key indicator dropped about 20% after the Reserve Bank last month announced the highest interest rates since 2011

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian households are the most persistently pessimistic they have been since the early-1990s recession, after a fourth rate rise this year.

Confidence among Australian consumers has plunged about 20% since the Reserve Bank of Australia lifted interest rates to the highest levels since 2011, according to the Westpac–Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index.
title: Australian consumer confidence plunges to worst level since 1990s after RBA rate rise

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: The party has voted to define Zionism as racist and back a single Palestinian state. But what does the policy mean, why has it caused alarm among Jewish members, and how will it impact the future of the Greens?

Good morning.

The Green party of England and Wales is in turmoil. Following a vote to adopt a policy that equates Zionism with racism, and calls for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state “with equal rights for all”, some Jewish members say they are considering whether they are welcome in the party.

RAF Fairford | No 10 has insisted the Gloucestershire base is secure a day after the US air force suddenly withdrew a dozen B-1 bombers that had been statione
title: Tuesday briefing: Why the Green party’s Zionism vote has caused a backlash

author: Nick Visser
description:
Mark Steele says he is ‘ashamed to be associated’ with the RSPCA Certified scheme, which badges 97% of chicken sold in Australia

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The vice-president of RSPCA New South Wales has left the animal welfare group, saying he is “sincerely ashamed” of the standards for RSPCA-certified chicken.

Mark Steele, a senior counsel who was a volunteer member of the board from 2021 and also served as a non-executive director of RSPCA Australia until March, issued a statement o
title: RSPCA NSW director quits over welfare standards for RSPCA-branded chicken

author: Amanda Meade
description:
Radio host gave financial help to teenager after starting correspondence with him at the age of 13, court hears

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When Alan Jones allegedly put his tongue inside the mouth of a 17-year-old and touched him on the bottom the teenager recoiled and withdrew to his ensuite where he scrubbed his mouth with a loofah, a Sydney court has heard.

“I felt violated and I felt gross,” the witness, who began corresponding with the broadcaster as a 13-year-old, said in his first day in the witness box where he is the fifth and final complainant in the lengthy trial of the former radio broadcaster.
title: ‘I felt violated’: witness alleges Alan Jones kissed him and put hand on his bottom when he was 17

author: Cecilia Nowell and agencies
description:
President’s U-turn comes after Democrats and Republicans condemned use of tax dollars for pro-Trump ads

Donald Trump said on Monday he would pay for taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads “with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”, a political action committee, after the television advertisements glorifying himself sparked a major backlash.

In a social media post, Trump characterized the ads, which cost at least $1.5m in federal funds, as “a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A.” and called them “a rather standard thing to do”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says Super Pac will pay for taxpayer-funded ads that sparked outcry

author: Cecilia Nowell and agencies
description:
Nidal Hasan sentenced to death by military jury in 2013 for carrying out deadly shooting attack at army base in Texas

Donald Trump has approved the execution by US army firing squad of Nidal Hasan, who was sentenced to death for killing 13 soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a social media post.

Hasan, who was an army psychiatrist, would become first US soldier to be executed by the US military in more than 60 years.

Continue reading...
title: Trump approves firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter, Pentagon says
